newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs off, pork bellies up on packer news.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs off, pork bellies up on packer news.

text.p: Further cutbacks in hog slaughter by at least one major packer pressured CME hog futures but boosted pork belly futures for sharp gains by the close, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.575 to 0.050 cent per lb lower with June off most at 83.475 cents. Pork bellies finished 2.075 cent higher to 0.650 lower with only March off and July up most at 89.025 cents.

IBP Inc Wednesday said it was reducing slaughter hours at its hog plants the remainder of this week and next week because of unfavorable margins, which weighed on hog futures and rallied pork belly values, traders said.

Cash hog prices were higher Wednesday which put packer margins deeper in the red and likely prompted the planned cutback in kills. Pork cutout values have been rising but the prices packers have had to pay for relatively tight supplies of market-ready hogs have been rising faster, they said.
"They (IBP) are the pace setters - whatever they do in the cash market" nobody will go against them, said Dave Maher with Securities Corporation of Iowa.
The June/July spread also turned on the packer news and technical weakness added to pressure.
However, losses in June were limited by continued talk of strength in the cash loin market, traders said.

Cash loin prices had been projected to top soon but demand appears to be running better than expected. Speculation continues that export demand for loins, possibly from Japan, has been very good. They could be buying for import ahead of the "gate" price being lowered after July 1, sources said.

Rand Financials, Rosenthal Collins and Cargill Investor Services sold. Lind-Waldock sold June and bought August. Spreaders bought July and sold June and also bought October and sold July, pit sources said.

In hog options, Rosenthal Collins bought out of the money July 72 puts early. Later, First Chicago sold June 80 and 81 puts while Lind-Waldock and Iowa Grain bought August 76 puts. Volatility was easier in June, pit sources added.

Early pressure in pork bellies from a bearish CME out-of-town report gave way to buying sparked by news of reduced kills which will limit fresh belly production. Late demand buoyed July into buy stops with closing stops sending prices sharply higher by the close, traders said.
LFG, Rand Financials and locals bought early with Refco buying late and Rand lightly selling back some July. Cargill and locals also bought, pit sources said.
